summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would remove the current legal cap of 1,500 gigalitres on how much water the Commonwealth can buy in the Murray-Darling Basin.
It does this by changing the Water Act 2007 so that no statutory barrier prevents additional water purchases if a review or the Murray-Darling Basin Authority recommends them.
The change also covers the 605 gigalitre 'supply projects', meaning purchases could be made if those projects fail to deliver expected environmental outcomes.
changes: Repeals the 1,500 gigalitre limit on Commonwealth surface water purchases.
Allows the Government to buy more water if a review or the Basin Authority advises it is needed.
Removes the legislative obstacle to buying water beyond the cap when supply projects underperform.
summary.affected: The Commonwealth Government, the Murray-Darling Basin Authority, and communities and environments in the Murray-Darling Basin.
